title: Budget and Revenue
text:
This page will look at the relationship between film production budgets and the revenue of worldwide box-office. Figure 1 displays the relationship between these two variables.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])

plt.xlabel("Production Budget (millions USD)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (millions USD)")
plt.title("Film Budget vs. Revenue")

plt.show()







Figure 1: Film production budgets and worldwide box-office revenue

title: Box Office Numbers
text: This website looks at a dataset of about 104 well-known films that are released between 1980 and 2025. The dataset includes production budgets, worldwide revenues, runtimes, and IMDb ratings of the films. The financial figures are approximate and have not been adjusted for inflation.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
This page look at if longer films tend to receive different IMDb ratings compared to shorter films. Figure 1 shows the relationship between the two variables of film runtime and IMDb rating.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])

plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb Rating")
plt.title("Film Runtime vs. IMDb Rating")

plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime and IMDb ratings

title: The Bond Films
text:
This page looks at how worldwide box-office revenue has changed across James Bond films. Figure 1 shows the revenue of James Bond films over time.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]
bond = bond.sort_values("year")

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")

plt.xlabel("Release Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide Revenue (millions USD)")
plt.title("James Bond Film Revenue Over Time")

plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide box-office revenue of James Bond films over time
